items.title: Multiple Vulnerabilities in Juniper Products Could Allow for Arbitrary Code Execution
items.summary: Multiple vulnerabilities have been discovered in Juniper Session Smart Router and Session Smart Conductor, the most severe of which could allow for arbitrary command execution as root. Session Smart Router is Juniper’s software-based SD-WAN router, and Session Smart Conductor is the management and orchestration platform for a fleet of these routers. Successful exploitation of the most severe of these vulnerabilities (CVE-2026-103406) could allow an unauthenticated remote attacker to execute arbitrary commands with root privileges on the affected Conductor. An attacker with root access could then install programs; view, change, or delete data; or create new accounts with full administrative rights. Because the Conductor manages the router fleet, a compromise could also put every managed site at risk.

items.title: Multiple Vulnerabilities in VMware Products Could Allow for Arbitrary Code Execution
items.summary: Multiple vulnerabilities have been discovered in VMware products, the most severe of which could allow for arbitrary code execution. Successful exploitation of the most severe of these vulnerabilities could result in arbitrary code execution. Depending on the privileges associated with the account, an attacker could then install programs; view, change, or delete data; or create new accounts with full user rights. Accounts configured to have fewer user rights on the system could be less impacted than those that operate with administrative user rights.

items.title: Multiple Vulnerabilities in Oracle Products Could Allow for Remote Code Execution
items.summary:
Multiple vulnerabilities have been discovered in Oracle products, the most severe of which could allow for remote code execution. Depending on the privileges associated with the account, an attacker could then install programs; view, change, or delete data; or create new accounts with full user rights. Accounts configured to have fewer user rights on the system could be less impacted than those that operate with administrative user rights.

Of particular concern is CVE-2026-114938, dubbed “Java4Shell,” a heap-based buffer overflow that could lead to remote code execution. Researchers attribute the flaw to the hardware-accelerated Base64 decoder in OpenJDK, while Oracle lists the affected component as the Compiler in Oracle Java SE and Oracle GraalVM for JDK. Because the Java runtime is embedded in many applications, containers, and appliances, affected software may be present in more places than organizations expect. Oracle has released updates that address this vulnerability, and organizations should prioritize identifying and updating every affected Java runtime in their environment.

items.title: Multiple Vulnerabilities in SAP Products Could Allow for Arbitrary Code Execution
items.summary:
Multiple vulnerabilities have been discovered in SAP Products, the most severe of which could allow for arbitrary code execution. 


  • SAP NetWeaver is SAP’s technology platform and application server stack (ABAP and Java) that underpins many SAP business applications, including ERP and S/4HANA.
  • SAP Web Dispatcher is a software load balancer and reverse proxy that receives web requests from the internet and forwards them to SAP application servers.
  • SAP Gateway is the component that exposes SAP data and business logic through OData services and manages RFC communication between SAP systems and external applications.
  • SAP ABAP Developer Tools is an eclipse-based development environment for writing, testing, and debugging ABAP code in SAP systems.
  • S4CRM is the customer relationship management software for SAP S/4HANA, covering sales, service, and marketing processes.
  • SAP Cloud SDK is a set of developer libraries (for languages such as Python and JavaScript) that simplify building applications that connect to SAP cloud services and AI capabilities.


Successful exploitation of the most severe of these vulnerabilities could allow the attacker to execute arbitrary code and fully compromise the system, resulting in a high impact on confidentiality, integrity and availability of the system.

items.title: Multiple Vulnerabilities in SonicWall SonicOS Could Allow for Authentication Bypass
items.summary: Multiple vulnerabilities have been discovered in SonicWall SonicOS, the most severe of which could allow for Authentication Bypass. SonicOS is the operating system that powers SonicWall firewalls and network security appliances. Successful exploitation of the most severe of these vulnerabilities could allow a remote unauthenticated attacker to perform unauthorized operations, gain elevated privileges, access sensitive information, or impact the integrity of the affected device. An attacker who successfully exploits these vulnerabilities could potentially modify device configurations, access protected resources, bypass security controls, or disrupt normal operations. Organizations with internet-accessible management interfaces may face increased risk from the vulnerabilities affecting the SonicOS management interface.

items.title: A Vulnerability in Cisco Secure Firewall ASA and FTD Could Allow for Denial of Service
items.summary:
A vulnerability has been discovered in Cisco Secure Firewall Adaptive Security Appliance (ASA) Software and Cisco Secure Firewall Threat Defense (FTD) Software that could allow for denial of service (DoS). Cisco Secure Firewall ASA and FTD provide firewall, VPN, and threat defense capabilities for enterprise environments. An attacker could exploit this vulnerability by sending a specially crafted request when connecting to a vulnerable SSL remote access VPN service that has secondary authentication configured on a tunnel group.


﻿Successful exploitation could cause the affected device to reload unexpectedly, resulting in a DoS condition and interruption of remote access services. Cisco has released software updates to address this vulnerability, and Cisco states that no workarounds address this vulnerability, though a temporary mitigation is available.

items.title: A Vulnerability in GitLab Could Allow for Remote Code Execution
items.summary: A vulnerability has been discovered in GitLab that could allow for remote code execution. GitLab is a DevOps platform that provides source code management, CI/CD pipelines, issue tracking, and collaboration tools in a single application for software development teams. Successful exploitation of this vulnerability could allow an unauthenticated attacker to execute arbitrary code on the GitLab server via a specially crafted regular expression in a CI/CD configuration. Successful exploitation could result in complete compromise of the affected system.

items.title: A Vulnerability in Brotli Library Could Allow for Remote Code Execution
items.summary: A vulnerability has been discovered in the Brotli library that could allow for remote code execution. Brotli is a compression algorithm developed by Google and commonly used to compress web content before it is sent over HTTP. Successful exploitation could allow an unauthenticated remote attacker to trigger memory corruption, disclose sensitive information, crash affected processes, or potentially achieve remote code execution (RCE). Web servers and applications that decompress Brotli data from untrusted sources, such as those running Node.js, may be affected.

items.title: Multiple Vulnerabilities in Apple Products Could Allow for Arbitrary Code Execution
items.summary:
Multiple vulnerabilities have been discovered in Apple products, the most severe of which could allow for arbitrary code execution.

  • iOS is a mobile operating system for mobile devices, including the iPhone and iPod touch.
  • iPadOS is the operating system for iPad devices.
  • macOS is the operating system for Mac computers.
  • tvOS is the operating system for Apple TV devices.
  • watchOS is the operating system for Apple Watch devices.
  • visionOS is the operating system for Apple Vision Pro.
  • Safari is a web browser available for macOS, iOS, and iPadOS.

Successful exploitation of the most severe of these vulnerabilities could allow for arbitrary code execution in the context of the affected application or, in some cases, with root, system, or kernel privileges. Depending on the privileges associated with the application or service, an attacker could then install programs; view, change, or delete data; or take further control of the affected device.
